carmen: Heads-up — eu-west2 tiny-slot fragmentation spiked overnight, lots of tiny-gang canaries failing with repeated evictions. eviction_rate panel shows periodic spikes tied to warm-pool churn.
lee: Are we sure it's fragmentation and not a NIC-induced eviction cascade? any recent rack egress events?
sanjay: Not a massive network event. We had a kernel security patch rolled on a subset of racks at 03:10 UTC which created a small rolling rebind. Combined with fractional tiny-gang requests + warmpool churn I think shelves became micro-islanded.
emma: Canary logs: scheduler returns "no nodes with contiguous GPU slots" then eventually schedules on heterogeneous variants which also get preempted. Example: ```kubectl describe pod tiny-canary-zz | grep -i -A3 "Events"```
ops-bot: incident created: INC-2026-1191 (eu-west2 micro-shelf fragmentation) priority=P2
carmen: Proposed short-term mitigation: 1) dry-run compaction to identify tiny-orphaned pods on warm nodes, 2) selective cordon+drain of low-contig free nodes (avoid large-gang disruption), 3) temporary autoscaler hold and 1x buffer instance added. Thoughts?
lee: I support compaction. Suggest the drain selector only evict pods with label "workload=tiny-gang" or pods with <0.25 gpu request to avoid evicting heavier jobs. We'll need a quick rollback playbook.
sanjay: I scripted a small coalescer: ```python
# scans node free slot bitmap and suggests nodes with <2 contiguous free slots for eviction
# supports --dry-run
``` gist incoming. We should pause cluster-autoscaler for the region before running.
emma: I'll mute the frag alert and hold the autoscaler for 45 minutes. Also provisioning: add 1xA10 as temporary buffer so the scheduler has breathing room during compaction.
carmen: Actioners: @sanjay publish gist + run dry-run in staging; @lee prepare drain commands and keep graceful period 60s; @emma mute alert and hold autoscaler, add buffer. Monitor eviction_rate and canary success.
sanjay: gist posted: https://gist.github.com/sanjay/defragment-coalesce - dry-run flag present. Running staging dry-run at 12:15 UTC.
lee: drain plan snippet: ```bash
kubectl cordon $NODE
kubectl drain $NODE --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --pod-selector='workload=tiny-gang' --grace-period=60
``` ensure eviction-monitoring enabled.
emma: Done: alert muted for 60m and autoscaler hold placed. Added temporary reserved A10 instance to warm pool.
sanjay: staging dry-run shows coalescer would consolidate ~20 nodes with negligible large-gang evictions (dry-run report attached). Requesting prod run at 12:40 UTC.
lee: approved. I'll watch pod-restores and have rollback steps ready. Post run-id when started.
carmen: Start window 12:40-13:10 UTC. If evictions persist >10/min abort and rollback.
ops-bot: alert muted: gpu-frag-eu-west2 (muted by emma)
sanjay: starting compaction run-id rc-2026-09 at 12:40 UTC now.
lee: keep an eye on inter-node network drop counters; if we see >5% packet drops revert.
emma: autoscaler still held. Monitoring panel pinned.
sanjay: run complete @12:55 UTC — coalescer reclaimed 18 nodes worth of contiguous slots, tiny-canary success rate jumped to 95%. Posting run log: https://logs.redwood/coalesce/rc-2026-09
carmen: Nice work. Leave muted alert for another 30m and keep autoscaler hold until 13:15 UTC. We'll follow up with a small postmortem and think about long-term fixes: smarter warm-pool placement, contiguous-slot-aware binpacking, and a ward for kernel patch rollouts.
lee: also proposal: introduce a "tiny-gang packing" taint that we can flip during maintenance windows to force denser placement.
sanjay: I'll open an RFC for a packing-aware scoring plugin and a scheduler prefilter to prefer contiguous slot nodes.
emma: Filed INC-2026-1191 -> updated with run details and mitigation notes. unmute scheduled at 13:45 UTC.
ops-bot: incident updated: INC-2026-1191 status=mitigated"
